description: Building a multi-agent generative AI crew that monitors astronaut health at the genomic, physiological, environmental, and behavioral level — and synthesizes everything into one intelligence the crew can actually talk to and interact. We are always hiring if people are interested.
summary:
AEGIS - Autonomous Expert Group of Integrated Space Health - is a mission control health guardian for crew that is bound for interplanetary missions like a Mars mission. There are six specialist agents that is watching a crew member around the clock. These agents are known as

1. SOLARIS - tracks radiation
2. GENE - tracks inflammation
3. PULSE - tracks vitals like oxygen, blood pressure, temperature and breathing
4. MIRROR - tracks sleep and mental health
5. OSSEO - tracks bone density.
6. ECHO - a private companion for crew member to chat to if they are bored or have mental issue

When there is a strain of alerts happening across systems, AEGIS forecasts a multi-system cascade alerts 2-3 minutes before it happens and guides the crew to take preventive actions. If prevention is not possible, it runs shelter and recovery protocols and issues recommendations that cite their NASA sources, leaving the call to the crew. Its reference ranges from real NASA datasets.
details:
Project Background and How it works?

  • Main Stack: https://13-219-198-186.sslip.io/aegis-mission-control.html
  • Monitoring Stack: https://13-219-198-186.sslip.io/grafana
  • Repo: https://github.com/kuriangeorgebinu/aegis-nasa-space-apps-2026

AEGIS - Autonomous Expert Group of Integrated Space Health - is a multi agent mission control dashboard for an interplanetary transit crew. There are six agents that watch each crew:

  1. SOLARIS - tracks radiation
  2. GENE - tracks inflammation
  3. PULSE - tracks vitals like oxygen, blood pressure, temperature and breathing
  4. MIRROR - tracks sleep and mental health
  5. OSSEO - tracks bone density.
  6. ECHO - a private companion for crew member to chat to if they are bored or have mental issue

Whenever there is an abnormality or strain in alerting, AEGIS forecasts a cascade about 2 to 3 minutes out then guides prevention or recovery onboard. The forecasting model is done using least squares linear regression which is applied on every metric and passed to the agent. Shown below are the early warning system and cascade alerts when things are getting serious

On a mars mission, a message to earth can take up to few minutes one way, so the crew cannot wait for mission control - AEGIS gives an early warning and the first response on board. It is built using FastAPI backend, a three.js 3D Cascade Map visualizing agent alerting as well as 266 NASA based document knowledge sources, hosted on AWS Lightsail. All the ranges of readings were simulated but the ranges are from actual NASA sources. Lastly, the agents provide active recommendations from the knowledge base using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with the documents stored in embedded chunks using ChromaDB vector store.

Benefits

The key benefit is time and clarity when it matters most. Instead of watching separate readings on their own, the crew gets one early warning minutes before a problem cascades, with the recommended action and the NASA source attached, so they can act on board instead of waiting for mission control. Catching issues early means small problems get handled before they turn into a bigger problem. The same system also watches sleep and mental health through MIRROR and ECHO, not just physical body. And because readings are compared against each crew member's own baseline, the alerts are personalized than generalized.

Impact

The intended impact is to keep crews safe on missions where help is far away. On a mars mission, a health problem that starts small can cascade into a bigger problem before mission control can even respond, so AEGIS puts the first line of defence on board with the crew. The same applies to other missions in the lunar or space station and even to remote communities on Earth where specialists are far away. By forecasting problems and almost immediate reaction, AEGIS aims to turn medical emergencies into manageable events.

Tech Stack

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI
  • Agents: rule-based using python; forecasting via least-squares linear regression
  • Frontend: three.js for the 3D Cascade Map, web dashboard
  • Knowledge Base / RAG: ChromaDB vector store using sentence transfromer embeddings along with 266 NASA documents
  • AI wording: a cloud AI service words the chat answers
  • Data Store: SQLite (vitals history and the trends)
  • Monitoring: Prometheus and Grafana
  • Hosting: AWS Lightsail provisioned with Terraform
  • CI/CD: Github Actions

How is the project creative ?

  • Forecasting instead of alerting: Most monitoring system just alarm when a reading crosses a line. AEGIS predicts the cascade minutes before it happens and spends that time on prevention
  • It watches convergence, not single metrics: The cascade idea itself - that radiation, immune, sleep and heart pressure complement and amplify each other. This is the key feature that whole design hangs on.
  • 3D Cascade map: Cross-system strain shown as a spatial picture; at the firing moment the whole map goes red together as shown in the demo.
  • Cited recommendation with Accept/Defer: The system advises, shows its NASA source and the crew decides - a human always stays in command.
  • ECHO: This is our companion agent sitting beside clinical agents. This agent treats mental health isolation as a health risk, not just an afterthought

The most creative aspect of this project is how it was made: by humans and AI developers working together as one team. The humans thought about the features and the big picture. The AI developers helped build the product — engineering, UX, and the agents — and assessed every part of it for the wow factor.

Factors or Considerations

  • No hardware readings: The readings are simulated but are anchored to the real NASA ranges based on NASA citations and papers and it shows as MODELLED/SIM right on dashboard. These are not actual hardware readings
  • Earth delay: Help from mission control arrives minutes late, so the design had to be autonomous on board, not ground guided
  • False alarms: A crew that gets alarms that are false they stop listening. That is why forecasts need a consistent trend.
  • People differ: IL-6 is judged against each crew member's own baseline not a one size population range.
  • Privacy: Mental health conversations with ECHO are private by default, which matters on a small crew.
  • Explanability over cleverness: Linear regression was a deliberate choice as every forecast can be traced to a slope, a threshold and a NASA source. There is no black box in the health system.
